post.summary: Delete the signed-in user and all their data
post.description: A hard delete: the user, their sessions, 2FA and every ledger row are removed, and the session cookie is cleared. `code` (a TOTP or backup code) is needed when the user has 2FA on. Wrong passwords and codes count toward the sign-in lockout.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

patch.summary: Rename an account or move it on or off budget
patch.description: A change of budget group takes effect today and is recorded as a dated system transaction. It moves the account into the default Budget (on) or Savings (off) pool.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

409.description: The name is taken, or the account is archived (code `account_archived`).

post.description: Only at zero balance. Otherwise the answer is `account_not_empty`, unless `settle` transfers the balance to another account in the same currency or writes it off first.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

409.description: The account still holds money (code `account_not_empty`), or the transfer target is archived.

get.summary: What archiving would do to today's figure
get.description: For each way of clearing the balance before archiving, how much today's left-today figure would drop, from the same projection as `/v1/today` with the settling entry added. A write-off from an on-budget account counts as spending; a transfer to an off-budget account lowers the allowance. `leftToday` is the figure now and each option's `leftTodayAfter` the figure once it is recorded. Nothing is recorded.

200.description: The drop in today's figure per option.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

get.summary: An account's balance day by day
get.description: The end-of-day balance in the account's currency for each of the last `days` days (7 to 365, 30 by default), today included, oldest first. Derived from the ledger by entry date, so a back-dated entry changes it at once.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

post.summary: Reconcile an account with the bank's balance
post.description: Compares the bank's balance with the ledger's at the end of `on` (today by default). Give either `balance` (negative for money owed) or, for a debt, `amountOwed` as the statement shows it (positive; compared as its negative). A match is recorded as the account's last reconciled date. A difference is only reported (`reconciled: false`) unless `adjust` is set: the difference is then posted on `on` as an expense to the Unrecorded category, or an income to Unrecorded income, and recorded in the same database transaction. With `expectedDifference`, an adjustment is refused (`reconcile_stale`) if the difference moved since the user saw it; if it dropped to zero, a match is recorded instead. The adjustment is an ordinary entry: undoing it also takes back that reconciliation.

200.description: The comparison and what was recorded.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

409.description: The account is archived (`account_archived`), the difference moved (`reconcile_stale`), or a category named Unrecorded has the other kind (`reconcile_category_conflict`).

get.summary: List pools with their accounts and balances
get.description: Every user has the default pools Budget (counts toward the daily number) and Savings (does not). A savings pool counts only when its own switch and the `countSavingsInDaily` setting are both on.

200.description: Pools, and archived ones on request.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.
Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

409.description: Another pool has this name (`pool_name_taken`).

patch.summary: Rename, switch or archive a pool
patch.description: The Budget pool always counts and neither default pool can be archived (`pool_fixed`). Only an empty pool is archived (`pool_not_empty`).

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

409.description: The name is taken, the pool is fixed or not empty.

put.summary: Move an account into a pool
put.description: Effective from `effectiveOn` (today by default) and recorded as a dated move; no entry changes. Figures for earlier days stay as they were, and a back-dated move corrects the days it covers.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

404.description: There is no such account or pool.

409.description: The account or the pool is archived.

get.summary: List savings goals with their progress
get.description: Progress is what the goal’s pool or account holds today, in the goal’s currency at the latest rate. Nothing is moved.

200.description: Goals, and archived ones on request.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

post.description: Give a savings pool or an account in one (`goal_not_savings` otherwise). A pool or account has one goal at a time (`goal_target_taken`).

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

404.description: There is no such pool or account.

409.description: The name or target is taken, or the target is not savings.

patch.summary: Rename, retarget, reschedule or archive a goal

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

409.description: The name or target is taken.

put.description: Who pays when spending passes what a budget has left, first to last: `free` for free money and budget IDs, the Buffer included. Bills are never used. What is left out is placed by default: free money first, the Buffer next, new budgets last.

200.description: The budgets with the new order.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

get.description: Every entry in the current period that went past what its budget had left, newest first, with what its own budget paid and who covered the rest. Computed from the ledger on each read, so a back-dated entry changes the figures at once. Amounts are in the default currency; currencies without a rate are left out and listed in `missingRates`. Budgets are virtual: they are tied to no account and nothing is moved. Cover is computed, never stored; no money moves.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

post.summary: Preview the cover for an expense
post.description: Works out, without recording anything, what an expense would take from its budget and from each cover source. `needsConfirmation` is true when the cover reaches a set-aside budget or the Buffer, or part of it is uncovered: show it in a warning colour and ask for a second tap. The entry is saved with `POST /v1/transactions`; nothing about the cover is sent with it.

200.description: The cover the entry would get.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

409.description: The account is archived.

put.summary: Choose how an entry is covered
put.description: A setting on the entry, not a ledger change: the entry and its postings stay as recorded. Each requested source covers at most what it had, and any shortfall left goes down the cover order, so an override cannot create money.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

delete.summary: Go back to the cover order for an entry

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

get.summary: Budgets for the current period, with free money
get.description: Computed from the ledger on each read, so a back-dated entry changes the figures at once. Amounts are in the default currency; currencies without a rate are left out and listed in `missingRates`. Budgets are virtual: they are tied to no account and nothing is moved. An entry counts toward at most one budget: a tag budget wins over a category budget, and a child category over its parent. Daily budgets stay in the daily number; set-aside ones, the Buffer included, are held out of it.

200.description: The budgets in use and what is free.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

post.description: On an expense category (a parent covers its children) or a tag, in the default currency. It counts from the current period. Leftover defaults to returning to free money for a daily budget and carrying over for a set-aside one.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

404.description: There is no such category or tag.

409.description: The name, category or tag already has a budget in use (`budget_taken`).

patch.description: A new amount applies from the current period; earlier periods keep theirs. The Buffer can be renamed and given an amount, and is always set aside and carried over (`budget_fixed`).

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

409.description: The name is taken, or the budget is fixed.

delete.description: By default ends it from the current period on: earlier periods keep their figures, and spending in this period counts as unbudgeted. With `mode=delete` a budget started in the current period is removed as if it was never planned; once a closed period used it, that is refused (`budget_used`) and it can only be ended. The Buffer can do neither (`budget_fixed`).

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

409.description: The Buffer cannot be removed (`budget_fixed`), or a closed period used the budget (`budget_used`).

get.description: Money owed to the user and money the user owes, one row per person per entry, with what was repaid or written off and what is left. `totals` are outstanding amounts in the default currency; currencies without a rate are left out and listed in `missingRates`. Money owed to the user lowers free money from the day it is lent but is never spending; money the user owes is reserved like a bill from the day it is recorded until it is paid. IOUs of an undone entry are left out.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

post.summary: Lend, borrow or split a bill
post.description: One entry and one IOU per person. `owed-to-me` posts what each person owes to the Receivables account, from the paying account; with `ownShare` it is a split bill: the user's share is an expense in its category and the rest is receivable, all from one payment. The cash lent is covered like a shortfall (free money, then the Buffer, then budgets) but is not spending. `owed-by-me` records money received and owed back. With an `Idempotency-Key` header, repeating a request returns what the key first created (200).

200.description: What this idempotency key created earlier.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

409.description: The account is archived.

get.description: Free-text names from earlier IOUs, most recently used first, for autocomplete. People are not contacts: a name is only text.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

post.description: Takes the body of `POST /v1/ious` for money owed to the user and works out, without recording anything, what the cash lent would take from free money, the Buffer and budgets. Same response as `POST /v1/budgets/cover-preview`.

200.description: The cover the entry would get.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

post.summary: Record a payment that settles IOUs
post.description: One entry that either names every IOU it settles and by how much (`settles`, never more than is left) or names a `person` and an `amount`, which settles that person's oldest open IOU first (by the day it was recorded), the surplus going to the next. All IOUs go the same way and are in the account's currency. Money paid back to the user refills what the loan's cover took, in reverse order, and the rest is free money again; money the user pays releases the reserve. Neither is spending. Undo the entry with `POST /v1/transactions/{id}/reverse` and the IOUs are owed again.

201.description: The entry and the IOUs it settled.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

404.description: There is no such IOU or account.

409.description: More than is still owed (`over_settled`).

post.summary: Split a logged expense with people
post.description: Turns a logged expense into a split bill, or a loan when people owe all of it. The expense is undone and replaced by one entry with the same account, amount, date, note and tags: each person's line is receivable and the rest is the user's own share, an expense in `categoryId` (the expense's category by default). Only a live expense in one category, in the account's currency and tied to no IOU, can be turned. With an `Idempotency-Key` header, repeating a request returns what the key first created (200).

200.description: What this idempotency key created earlier.

201.description: The undo, the new entry and its IOUs.

400.description: The request is invalid, people owe more than the expense (`owed_exceeds_total`), or in another currency (`currency_mismatch`).

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

409.description: Not a live plain expense (`not_plain_expense`), or the account is archived.

post.summary: Write off what is still owed to the user
post.description: Turns the remainder into an expense in the chosen category. No cash moves, so it is not spending against the day. Allowed from `writeOffFrom` on (the `iouWriteOffAfterDays` setting after the due date, or after the day it was recorded when there is none).

201.description: The entry and the settled IOU.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

409.description: Already settled, or money the user owes.

patch.summary: Correct a name or set a due date
patch.description: Only the name and the due date can change; the amount and the entry are part of the ledger.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

get.description: The savings line first (the `payYourselfFirst` setting: a fixed amount or a share of the paycheck), then this period's budgets prefilled with their plan, and a suggestion for every category without a budget that has been spending, averaged over up to three past cycles. Computed from the ledger on each read. Amounts are in the default currency; currencies without a rate are left out and listed in `missingRates`.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

post.summary: Confirm the payday sheet in one step
post.description: Sets the amount of each listed budget from this period on, plans a budget for each listed category, and, when `savings` is given, records the savings line as one transfer from the first account to the second. Everything is checked before anything is written. The transfer has an idempotency key for the cycle, so repeating the call records no second transfer.

200.description: The savings entry and the budgets.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

404.description: A budget, category or account does not exist.

409.description: A category already has a budget in use.

get.description: Savings (accounts that do not count toward the daily number) against a target of `emergencyMonths` months of average expenses, with the usual three and six months. The average is per cycle over up to three past cycles. Computed from the ledger on each read. Amounts are in the default currency; currencies without a rate are left out and listed in `missingRates`.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

get.summary: Net worth and its daily series
get.description: Every account, savings included, with debts counted by their sign. `days` (default 30) sets the length of the series, which ends today. Computed from the ledger on each read. Amounts are in the default currency; currencies without a rate are left out and listed in `missingRates`.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

get.description: The seven days ending today against the seven before, the biggest categories, and where the budgets stand. Payments linked to a reserved bill and reconcile adjustments are not counted as spending. Computed from the ledger on each read. Amounts are in the default currency; currencies without a rate are left out and listed in `missingRates`.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

get.description: Parents come before their subcategories. Merged categories are left out unless asked for.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.
Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

get.summary: One category, including a merged one

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

409.description: Another category at this level has this name.

delete.summary: Delete a category, or merge it into another
delete.description: A category that entries use must be merged (`mergeInto`); it then stays only to resolve those entries.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

409.description: The category is in use (code `category_in_use`) or has subcategories (code `category_has_children`).

Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

409.description: A tag with this name exists.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

404.description: The category or tag filter does not exist.

post.summary: Record an expense, income or transfer
post.description: Cross-currency entries record both amounts. With an `Idempotency-Key` header, repeating a request returns the entry the key first created (200) instead of recording another.

200.description: The entry this idempotency key created earlier.

400.description: The request is invalid, or the entry would break a ledger rule (for example `unbalanced` or `currency_mismatch`). Nothing is written.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

404.description: There is no such entry or account.

409.description: An account is archived (code `account_archived`).

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

404.description: There is no such entry or account.

post.description: Posts a reversal that negates every posting and carries the original date, so past figures are corrected too. Nothing is deleted.

400.description: The request is invalid, or the entry would break a ledger rule (for example `unbalanced` or `currency_mismatch`). Nothing is written.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

404.description: There is no such entry or account.

409.description: Already undone (`already_reversed`), an undo (`reversal_of_reversal`), or on an archived account.

post.description: Records a copy of an undone entry with its date, category, note, tags and postings. The entry and its undo stay as they are.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

404.description: There is no such entry or account.

409.description: Not undone (`not_undone`), already restored (`already_restored`), an undo or budget switch, or on an archived account.

post.description: Posts a reversal of the entry plus the replacement described by the body. Nothing is updated in place. The replacement points at the entry it replaced (`replacesId`), and the list leaves the earlier version and its undo out: an edit is not a delete.

400.description: The request is invalid, or the entry would break a ledger rule (for example `unbalanced` or `currency_mismatch`). Nothing is written.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

404.description: There is no such entry or account.

409.description: Already undone, an undo, or on an archived account.

post.summary: Go back to an earlier version of an edited entry
post.description: The entry as it stands now is replaced by a copy of this earlier version, with its date, category, note, tags and postings: a reversal plus the copy, as for any edit.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

404.description: There is no such entry or account.

409.description: Not an earlier version (`not_replaced`), the entry was deleted since (`entry_deleted`), it lends, borrows or settles an IOU (`iou_entry`), or it is on an archived account.

post.summary: Move an entry within its day
post.description: Places the entry right after `afterId`, or first in its day when that is null. Only its place changes: the entry itself, its date and its amounts stay as recorded. Entries with a time of day stay in time order. Projections that take entries in order, such as budget cover, follow the new order.

200.description: The day's entries in their new order.

400.description: `afterId` is on another day (`different_day`) or is the entry itself.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

404.description: There is no such entry or account.

409.description: The entry has a time and the move would put it out of time order (`out_of_time_order`).

get.description: Derived from the ledger by entry date for the user's calendar day, so a back-dated entry changes them at once. Amounts are in the default currency; currencies without a rate are left out and listed in `missingRates`. `allocation` splits the open cycle's on-budget start into bills paid, money moved to savings, spending, bills set aside and free money; the five parts add up to `start` exactly.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.
Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

patch.description: Switching the default currency changes how figures are reported, never the entries. `paydayRule` is `fixed` (the default: `paydayDay` of the month), `last-working-day` (the last Monday to Friday of the month) or `manual` (set `paydayOverride` each cycle; `paydayDay` stands in until then). `paydayOverride: null` clears the override.

400.description: The request is invalid, or the locale (`invalid_locale`) or time zone (`invalid_time_zone`) is unknown.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

get.description: Computed from the ledger on each read, so a back-dated entry changes a past cycle at once. Amounts are in the default currency at the rate on the cycle's last day; currencies without a rate are left out and listed in `missingRates`. A past cycle is `amended` when an entry dated in it was recorded after the paycheck that closed it.

200.description: The current cycle, then the past ones.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

get.summary: One cycle's figures day by day
get.description: One row per day from the day the cycle opened to the day before payday (through today while payday is overdue, or to the day before it closed). Figures use the same projection as `/v1/today`, so today's row matches it. `spent` and `cumulativeSpent` leave out what pace leaves out; rows after today are null except `pace`, which spreads `budget` (pace spending so far plus what is available) evenly over the cycle, rounded down. Amounts are in the default currency at each day's rate.

200.description: The days of the cycle that opened on that day.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

404.description: No cycle opened on that day (`cycle_not_found`).

get.description: Computed from the ledger on each read, so a back-dated entry changes a past cycle at once. Amounts are in the default currency at the rate on the cycle's last day; currencies without a rate are left out and listed in `missingRates`. `amendments` lists the entries that amended it.

200.description: The cycle that opened on that day.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

404.description: No cycle opened on that day (`cycle_not_found`).

get.summary: Spending per day and what falls due
get.description: One row per day from `from` through `to` (at most 62 days; the current calendar month when both are left out). `spent` is the pace spending of the day, in the default currency at the rate of that day, with payments linked to a bill and reconcile adjustments left out; it is null after today. `heat` scales it from 0 to 4 against the busiest day of the range. `bills` lists bills due that day, `payday` marks a paycheck that arrived or is expected, and `ious` lists unsettled IOUs due. Computed from the ledger on each read.

400.description: The range is empty or longer than 62 days (`invalid_range`).

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

get.summary: Spending and income per category for a period
get.description: Top-level categories with their subcategories rolled up, largest first, for a payday cycle (`period=cycle`, the open one unless `cycle` names the day another opened) or a calendar month (`period=month`, the current one unless `month` is given). Computed from the ledger on each read, in the default currency at the rate on the last day of the period; currencies without a rate are left out and listed in `missingRates`. A merged category counts as the one it was merged into. With `series=N` the response also has `series`: spending per top-level category (subcategories counted in their parent, as above) for the N consecutive cycles or months ending with the selected one, oldest first, each in the default currency at the rate on that period's last day. `points` and `totals` line up with `periods`; fewer periods come back when history is shorter.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

404.description: No cycle opened on that day (`cycle_not_found`).

get.description: The payees with the most spending for a payday cycle (`period=cycle`, the open one unless `cycle` names the day another opened) or a calendar month (`period=month`, the current one unless `month` is given). A payee is an entry's note, compared ignoring case and extra spaces. Each currency is ranked on its own, largest total first, and nothing is converted or added across currencies. Counts are entries; a split is one entry. Transfers, income, undone entries and reconcile adjustments are left out; entries without a note are reported as `unnamed`. `limit` caps the payees listed per currency and `more` says how many were cut. Computed from the ledger on each read.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

404.description: No cycle opened on that day (`cycle_not_found`).

get.description: Bills due today or tomorrow, IOUs due or overdue (weekly while overdue) and the weekly review, newest first, at most 50, with how many are unread. The server creates them on a timer; each is created once.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

post.description: The given IDs, or every unread reminder when `ids` is left out.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

get.summary: The key a browser subscribes with
get.description: The instance VAPID public key, generated the first time the server started. Web Push is off until a user subscribes on a device.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.
Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

post.summary: Turn push notifications on for a device
post.description: Stores the browser's push subscription. Notifications then go through the browser vendor's push service. The endpoint must be https; the server only connects to it if it resolves to public addresses.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

delete.summary: Turn push notifications off for a device

204.description: Removed, or it was not there.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

post.description: Sends one notification to every device this user subscribed. A device the push service no longer knows is removed.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

get.description: `system` follows the device light or dark preference. `light` and `dark` name the theme used for each scheme: a shipped theme id or a custom theme id. Before any change, they are Catppuccin Latte and Mocha. The earlier ids `light` and `dark` read as `allotr-classic-light` and `allotr-classic-dark`.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

put.description: A slot left out keeps its current theme.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

422.description: A slot names an unknown theme (`theme_not_found`) or one of the other scheme (`theme_scheme_mismatch`).

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

post.description: Send a v2 body, `{ name, scheme, family?, palette, roles? }`: the palette is completed and each role resolved with contrast fitting (ADR 0016). A v1 body, `{ name, scheme, tokens }`, is still accepted, checked by the v1 contrast pairs and converted; it is deprecated, and the response carries a `Deprecation` header. Responses are v2 and keep `tokens` for clients before v2: the tokens sent, or ones taken from the resolved roles.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

409.description: The name is taken (`theme_name_taken`) or the limit of custom themes is reached (`theme_limit`).

422.description: Some colours fail WCAG 2.2 AA (`theme_contrast`). For a v2 body, `errors` lists each role that cannot meet its contrast at `/roles/<role>` (a role the body sets, or an unknown slot), or at `/palette` (a role from the default map); for a v1 body, each failing pair at `/tokens/<foreground>`.

put.description: Send a v2 body, `{ name, scheme, family?, palette, roles? }`: the palette is completed and each role resolved with contrast fitting (ADR 0016). A v1 body, `{ name, scheme, tokens }`, is still accepted, checked by the v1 contrast pairs and converted; it is deprecated, and the response carries a `Deprecation` header. Responses are v2 and keep `tokens` for clients before v2: the tokens sent, or ones taken from the resolved roles. If the scheme changes while the theme is in use, that slot goes back to its default theme.

post.summary: Read a theme from a URL
post.description: Only while an admin allows it (`themeUrlImport`). The server fetches the https address, which must resolve only to public addresses, with no redirects, a 5 s timeout and a 64 KB cap, and reads it as a theme file, palette file or terminal colour config. The answer is the parsed themes as v2 files; nothing is saved. At most 10 a user an hour.

400.description: The address is refused before fetching (`theme_url_refused`): not https, credentials in it, or it resolves to a non-public address; `errors` gives the reason at `/url`.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

422.description: What the address holds is not a theme (`theme_unreadable`).

429.description: Too many imports from a URL (`rate_limited`).

502.description: The fetch failed (`theme_url_fetch_failed`): a redirect, an error status, too large, or too slow.

post.description: Each active bill due in the cycle is reserved from the day the cycle opens until it is marked paid. A bill with a `price` in another currency reserves `amount` until a payment records what it took, then what its latest payment took.

400.description: The request is invalid, the amount is not in the account's currency (`currency_mismatch`), the price is (`price_same_currency`), or the category is not an expense category (`invalid_category`).

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

409.description: The account is archived (`account_archived`).

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

patch.description: An inactive bill is no longer reserved. `accountId` moves the bill to another open account; its currency must match the amount and differ from the price. `price: null` removes the price.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

delete.description: Removes the bill and its payment marks. Entries stay.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

post.description: Releases the reserve for that due date from `paidOn`. Give `paid` to record the payment: an expense of that amount from the bill's account, dated `paidOn` (today when omitted), with the bill's price (or `price`) and category (or `categoryId`). Or link the entry that already paid it with `transactionId`: one in effect that took money out of the bill's account and pays no other due date; `paidOn` is then the entry's date when omitted.

400.description: The request is invalid, the bill is not due that day (`not_a_due_date`), `paid` is not in the account's currency (`currency_mismatch`), there is no category to record it under (`category_required`), or the linked entry took nothing from the bill's account (`not_a_bill_payment`).

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

404.description: There is no such bill or entry.

409.description: That due date is already paid (`bill_already_paid`), or the linked entry was undone (`transaction_undone`) or already pays a bill (`transaction_already_linked`).

delete.description: The due date is reserved again. An entry recorded with the mark is undone with it; a linked entry stays.

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

404.description: There is no such bill, or that due date is not paid.

post.summary: Fill an empty ledger from a bundle
post.description: Applies the whole bundle in one database transaction: all of it or none of it. Items refer to each other by name. Each error names the failing item as a JSON Pointer in `errors[].path`.

400.description: The bundle is invalid (`invalid_bundle`), of another version (`unsupported_bundle_version`), names something that does not exist (`invalid_reference`), or an item was refused while applying (its usual code).

403.description: Not allowed, or two-factor enrolment is required first.

409.description: The ledger already has accounts, entries, bills or rates (`ledger_not_empty`), or an item conflicts.

413.description: The bundle is larger than 10 MB.
